subject: imGHUM status: completion works, hands are the weak spot
body:
Lucia, Daniela,

Status. Integration is done and the SDF-query benchmarks look strong - differentiable signed-distance evaluation is fast enough that completion fitting runs at interactive-adjacent speeds on a single GPU. On the internal capture set, body-scan completion recovers plausible geometry on 83% of our partial-scan test cases, versus 61% for the current heuristic pipeline, and the implicit semantics give us surface labeling for free, which the cleanup tooling team immediately asked for.

Weak spot: hands. On scans where fingers are partially occluded, the hand models produce anatomically plausible but wrong finger poses in ~30% of cases - the latent prior dominates when observations are thin, exactly as you'd expect from a generative model. Efe's take is that for the scan-cleanup product this is acceptable if we flag low-confidence hand regions instead of silently completing them; confidence comes cheap from the observation coverage stats.

Decision needed by mid-June: ship v1 with flagged-hands, or hold for a hand-specific fitting pass. My recommendation is flag-and-ship.

Yara
